tweets.text: The one type of question I get asked the most after affordability questions (primarily related to housing, healthcare, and energy costs), are questions related to election integrity. And it’s not just Republican or conservative voters asking. I primarily talk to unenrolled voters - aka independent voters - who make up 66.6% of registered voters in MA. They ask if I can guarantee none of the 400K illegal migrants living in MA will vote. Of course, there is no way for me to guarantee that not a single non-citizen will vote in the upcoming election. What I can say is that a significant number of voters have lost faith and confidence in the electoral process - regardless of who’s to blame or why. And when voters lack confidence in election results, it poses a serious threat to our republic. Over 80% of Americans support voter ID laws. Yet @EdMarkey calls them racist. That's rich coming from a politician who spent his first decade in office supporting actual racist policies. Of course, over 70% of black Americans also believe in voter ID. I’m sure they appreciate a guy - who fought to keep them from being bused to white schools - and who fought to protect one of the most racist Universities in the country - and who was still referring to black Americans as “coloreds” as recently as 2010 - is now speaking for them deciding what he believes to be racist - even if they overwhelmingly disagree with it. We need to dial down the bullshit rhetoric when it comes to elections and have an honest discussion. Some will say Trump started it. Trump supporters will say @HillaryClinton started it by calling Trump an illegitimate president who was elected with the help of Russian interference. I didn’t vote for either of them, and at this point, it doesn’t matter who started it. What matters is how do we fix it and restore confidence in the process. France is a very liberal country and they banned mail-in voting in the 1970s because of the potential for fraud. Liberal countries including ones with a higher voter turnout than America require Voter ID (eg, France, Greece, Italy, Mexico, Germany). Hence, we should be able to discuss these issues without being labeled a racist or xenophobe! The fact that Congress can’t work together and make a bipartisan law on an issue 80% of Americans support - clearly demonstrates why we should vote every incumbent out and start fresh.

tweets.text: RT @Kaiz_294: Zcash brought privacy back into the center of the crypto conversation Mert connects the renewed interest in privacy directly to Zcash's rise from the top 100 into the top 10. "Zcash, going from the top 100 to the top 10, played quite a large role in that." "Crypto, attention, liquidity equals price action." "It is one of the things left in finance that is player versus environment." "If I have privacy, and Laura, you have privacy, that's good for both of us." Price action creates attention. Attention brings liquidity, new participants and more opportunities for teams building in the sector. That's where Mert's PvE idea becomes interesting. Most financial markets are fundamentally competitive. One participant's gain can come from another participant's loss. Privacy works differently. If two people gain stronger financial privacy, both benefit from it. The utility expands across the network instead of requiring users to compete against each other for the same outcome. Zcash's recent rise therefore did more than move the token higher. It put privacy back on the industry's radar and gave the entire sector a new source of attention. Zcash moved. Privacy got attention. A forgotten crypto primitive started becoming a market again. w/ @mert
